data.name: Lahu
data.gender_notes: Lahu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Lahu is the name of a demon who was cursed by Lord Shiva to turn red when he touched water. This name is believed to bestow courage and strength. The name Lahu carries the meaning “Red” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lahu usually hope their child will grow to embody red and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embraces the courage and strength of the divine demon Lahu.
data.etymology: Lahu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Red.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lahu total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Lahu was a king of the Vatsa kingdom in ancient India during the Magadha Empire period. He is best known for his alliance with Chandragupta Maurya, which helped him expand his territories and solidify his rule.

Another Lahu is mentioned as a king in the Mahabharata epic, who ruled over the Kalinga kingdom around the 3rd century BC. He is most famous for his war with Bhagadatta, which ended in a stalemate due to divine intervention.
